sections.h2: The state WMA limit has risen at every revision, doubling in 2016

chart.title: The limit has risen at each revision, and the 2026 proposal adds 11.2% more
chart.sub: Ways-and-means limit for all states, Rs crore.

sections.means: The limit has grown at each revision, and the 2026 committee would base future limits on revenue receipts and cap yearly rises at 4%.
sections.todo: The committee asks states to spread their borrowing through the year and use SDF, WMA and overdraft only for genuine short gaps.

sections.h2: Use of the WMA window fell for two years running, while the SDF rose

chart.title: WMA use fell from 2,029 to 1,586 state-days, while SDF use rose to 3,008
chart.sub: WMA state-days for all states, by financial year.

sections.means: Fewer state-days on WMA means fewer states relying on the RBI for short gaps, while the cheaper SDF took on more of the load.
sections.todo: States that still lean on WMA should move short gaps to the SDF, which the proposal would also make easier to use, rather than overdraw.

sections.h2: Idle state cash in April–May 2026 was 2.6–3.3 times the whole WMA limit

chart.title: States held Rs 1.6–2 lakh crore in idle treasury bills each month in spring 2026
chart.sub: Average monthly state holdings in 14-day intermediate treasury bills, Rs lakh crore.

sections.means: Borrowing bunched at year-end leaves cash idle at the start of the next year, while a handful of states overdraw at higher rates.
sections.todo: States should spread market borrowing across the year so that idle cash and short-term RBI credit are both needed less.
